security_audit.summary: All 70 static findings are false positives involving public API access, documented cache storage, Markdown syntax, or readable Japanese text. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or unauthorized data exfiltration. Two semantic findings identify host-timezone errors and misleading safe classifications when observations contain no valid values.

remediation.issue: Default API timestamps use host-local time instead of Japan Standard Time.
remediation.suggestion: Use timezone-aware Asia/Tokyo timestamps for forecast announcements and survey dates. Test UTC hosts and JST date boundaries.

remediation.issue: Survey summaries report a safe zero maximum when every outdoor observation is invalid.
remediation.suggestion: Track valid, finite observations and report unavailable data when none exist. Never assign a risk category to missing readings.

semantic_findings.title: Host Timezone Can Select Stale Heat Forecasts
semantic_findings.description: Default forecast announcements and survey dates use naive host-local timestamps, although the API expects JST. Non-JST hosts can retrieve older forecasts or the wrong observation date, misleading heat-risk decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper uses datetime.now() without timezone conversion. A local check selected the previous day's 17:00 announcement at 03:30 UTC, instead of the current day's 11:00 JST announcement.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Observations Produce a Misleading Safe Maximum
semantic_findings.description: The survey maximum starts at zero and remains zero when every outdoor reading is missing or nonnumeric. The summary then labels the day safe despite having no valid observations, potentially encouraging unsafe heat exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A mocked survey containing an empty outdoor reading produced a 0.0 maximum with the safe category. The code does not track whether any valid observations exist.

content.user_title: Check Japan Heat Risk with WBGT Data
content.value_statement: Heat-risk planning requires location-specific readings with clear timestamps. This skill retrieves Japanese government WBGT forecasts and observations, matches stations, and presents five risk categories.
actual_capabilities: Search station names and identify stations offering measured observations.
Find the nearest station from latitude and longitude using geographic distance.
Retrieve station forecasts in three-hour intervals and convert tenths into degrees Celsius.
Retrieve daily estimated and measured observations and summarize outdoor WBGT values.
Map WBGT values to five documented heat-risk categories.
Cache the public station master locally and refresh it on request.
limitations: Requires network access for forecasts, observations, and initial station-master retrieval; data can be delayed or unavailable outside the service season.
Default dates and forecast announcements depend on host-local time; non-JST hosts require explicit JST dates and announcement times.
The helper can report a safe daily maximum when all outdoor readings are invalid; verify valid observations before interpreting summaries.
Does not provide medical diagnosis, exercise clearance, emergency transport statistics, or special heatstroke alert text.

prompt_templates.prompt: Find stations with names containing Tokyo. Show their identifiers and whether measured observations are available. Use the Japanese station name if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Daily Observations
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve station 44132 observations for 2026-09-01. Show hourly outdoor readings and risk categories. Report a daily maximum only when valid readings exist.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Nearby Forecast
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the nearest station to latitude 35.68, longitude 139.69. Verify the latest JST announcement explicitly and summarize forecast risk, distance, and data limitations.

best_practices: Include station identity, observation or forecast time, and JST announcement time in every result.
Validate API status and available readings; distinguish missing data from low heat risk.
Confirm JST dates explicitly on non-JST hosts and consult official activity guidance before making safety decisions.
anti_patterns: Presenting historical forecasts or empty responses as current conditions.
Treating a missing-data zero maximum as proof that outdoor activity is safe.
Using JIS prefecture codes as API prefecture identifiers instead of resolving station numbers.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The documented Japanese government WBGT API provides public data without an API key, login, or registration.

faq.question: Which locations are covered?
faq.answer: The documented station master contains 865 locations across Japan. Search station names or supply coordinates to choose a nearby station.

faq.question: How frequently are forecasts published?
faq.answer: The skill documents announcements at 05:00, 11:00, and 17:00 JST, with forecast values in three-hour intervals.

faq.question: Where does the helper store data?
faq.answer: It caches station metadata in ~/.cache/kurashi-skill/heatstroke/. The refresh option downloads a new station master; forecasts and observations require API requests.

faq.question: What does an empty response mean?
faq.answer: Data may be unavailable outside the service season, delayed, or requested for an incorrect announcement time. Empty results do not indicate safe conditions.

faq.question: Can this determine whether exercise is safe?
faq.answer: No. WBGT is a general heat-risk indicator, not individual medical advice. Consult official activity guidance and verify valid readings and timestamps.
